items.pronunciation_notes: The स्ट cluster is retroflex and the vowel comes only after it: sṭe-shan.

learn.title_en: स्टेशन, and the verb for arriving
learn.explanation_en: स्टेशन is borrowed straight from English, written with a retroflex ट as loanwords always are, and it is masculine and Class 2. The verb worth learning alongside it is पहुँचना, to reach or arrive — and it is intransitive, which means every tense in Module 7 is available to you including the perfective. मैं स्टेशन पहुँचा, I reached the station. After a run of transitive collocations you could only use in the present, this one is fully open.

examples.note: The bare perfective — पहुँचना is intransitive, so no ने is needed.
A question you will need before you need almost anything else.

examples.english: there are a lot of people at the station
examples.note: स्टेशन is oblique before पर, though Class 2 shows nothing.

common_error.why_en: पहुँचना is intransitive, so the subject stays plain. ने only ever appears with transitive verbs in the perfective.

practice.question: स्टेशन
practice.explanation_en: स्टेशन is a station, masculine, and unchanged in the plural.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with स्टेशन when you get there?
game.explanation_en: स्टेशन पहुँचना — to reach the station. पहुँचना is intransitive.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ड़ is a single flap of the curled tongue, and the final क is barely voiced: sa-ṛak.

learn.explanation_en: Both translate as road and they are not the same thing. सड़क is the physical street — tarmac, traffic, something you cross. रास्ता is the route or the way, which can be abstract: रास्ता पूछना is asking for directions, not for a street. So you cross a सड़क and you find a रास्ता. सड़क is feminine and flagged, Class 5, with the plural सड़कें. Its collocation is पार करना, to cross, which is transitive.

examples.note: The तुम imperative — करना is transitive, so the perfective is not yet available.

examples.english: there are cars on the road
examples.note: सड़क is oblique before पर, and Class 5 shows nothing in the singular.
लंबी is feminine, which proves सड़क is.

common_error.why_en: सड़क is feminine. The consonant ending predicts nothing, which is exactly why it carries a flag.

practice.question: सड़क
practice.explanation_en: सड़क is the physical street. रास्ता is the way or route.

game.explanation_en: सड़क पार करना — to cross the road. रास्ता is what you ask for.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted ज़ is a z, so the word ends in a buzz rather than a j: ja-haaz.

learn.title_en: जहाज़ was a ship before it was a plane
learn.explanation_en: जहाज़ originally meant a ship, and when aircraft arrived Hindi called them हवाई जहाज़ — sky-ships. In ordinary speech the हवाई is usually dropped, so जहाज़ on its own now means a plane far more often than a boat. Masculine, flagged, and written with a dotted ज़ that is pronounced as a z. The verb is उड़ना, to fly, which is intransitive.

examples.note: उड़ना is intransitive, so जहाज़ is a plain subject.
से for the means of travel, as with बस से.
The perfective of पहुँचना, which is safe because it is intransitive.

common_error.why_en: चलना is for things that move along the ground. A plane flies, so the verb is उड़ना.

practice.question: जहाज़
practice.explanation_en: जहाज़ is a plane in modern usage, and originally a ship.

game.explanation_en: जहाज़ उड़ना — a plane flies. चलना belongs to things that travel on the ground.

summary.recap_en: सड़क and रास्ता both translate as road and mean different things — one is the street, the other the route. पहुँचना is intransitive, so it is the first travel verb whose perfective you can actually use.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the formal word for a journey, what you carry on it, and how far away things are.

items.pronunciation_notes: The त्र is a single cluster with no vowel between the त and the र: yaa-traa.

learn.title_en: The third feminine noun ending in -ा
learn.explanation_en: यात्रा is a journey, and it is the formal counterpart of सफ़र — the word on a railway announcement, a news report or a printed sign, where सफ़र is what you say in conversation. Both mean the same thing and neither is better; they belong to different registers. Note the ending: यात्रा is feminine and ends in -ा, joining चिंता and हवा. All three are Sanskrit borrowings, which is the closest thing to a pattern here, and it is a hint rather than a rule.

examples.note: अच्छी and थी are both feminine, which proves यात्रा is.
करना is transitive, so the habitual is used here rather than the perfective.
A set phrase, said as someone leaves. शुभ is unmarked and never changes.

common_error.why_en: The -ा ending suggests masculine and is wrong. यात्रा is feminine, like चिंता and हवा.

practice.question: यात्रा
practice.explanation_en: यात्रा is a journey — the formal word, where सफ़र is the conversational one.

game.explanation_en: यात्रा करना — the same verb that goes with सफ़र.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two long aa vowels, evenly weighted: saa-maan.

learn.title_en: सामान is always singular, however much of it there is
learn.explanation_en: सामान covers luggage, belongings, goods, equipment, and the general stuff of a household. It is uncountable in Hindi — there is no plural — so even a mountain of suitcases is सामान and takes a singular verb: सामान भारी है. That catches English speakers, who expect a plural for bags. Masculine and flagged. The verb is रखना, to put or keep, which is transitive.

examples.note: The तुम imperative — रखना is transitive.
Singular verb, however many bags there are.
मेरा is masculine, agreeing with सामान.

common_error.why_en: सामान has no plural, so the verb stays singular no matter how many pieces you are carrying.

practice.question: सामान
practice.explanation_en: सामान is luggage or belongings, and it has no plural.

game.explanation_en: सामान रखना — to put or keep luggage.

items.pronunciation_notes: One long syllable with a rolled r at the end: duur.

learn.title_en: दूर and पास, and the से that goes with them
learn.explanation_en: दूर is far and पास is near, and both are unmarked, so neither ever changes. The thing to learn is what they take: दूर uses से for what you are far from, and पास uses के. स्टेशन से दूर, far from the station; स्टेशन के पास, near the station. You already met के पास in Module 6 as the way Hindi says have, and this is the same phrase doing its literal job.

examples.note: The bare adjective with होना.

examples.english: the station is far from here
examples.note: से marks what you are measuring from.
पास takes के, not से — the two opposites do not match.

common_error.why_en: दूर takes से. Copying पास's के across is the natural mistake, since the two words are opposites.

practice.question: दूर
practice.explanation_en: दूर is far, and it never changes its form.

game.explanation_en: स्टेशन से दूर. पास takes के instead, which is worth keeping straight.

summary.recap_en: यात्रा is the third feminine noun in this module to end in -ा, and all three are Sanskrit borrowings — a hint rather than a rule. सामान has no plural at all, and दूर takes से while its opposite पास takes के.
summary.next_up_en: Next: arriving, being late, and going straight on — which completes the travel block.

items.pronunciation_notes: The nasal sits on the middle syllable as a hum: pa-huṁch-naa.

learn.title_en: पहुँचना — intransitive, so everything is available
learn.explanation_en: पहुँचना means to arrive or reach, and it is intransitive: the subject stays plain and no ने ever appears. That matters because it is the one travel verb whose whole tense grid you can use right now. मैं पहुँचा, मैं पहुँच रहा हूँ, मैं पहुँचूँगा — all of them work. Note also that the destination usually takes no postposition at all, exactly like जाना: घर पहुँचना, स्टेशन पहुँचना.

examples.note: The bare perfective, and the destination takes no postposition.
देर से means late, and the verb agrees with the feminine subject.
The plural future, from Module 7.

common_error.why_en: Like जाना and आना, पहुँचना takes its destination bare. Adding को is a translation from English.

practice.question: पहुँचना
practice.explanation_en: पहुँचना is to arrive or reach, and it is intransitive.

game.question_en: Which noun most naturally goes with पहुँचना?
game.explanation_en: स्टेशन पहुँचना — you arrive at a place, and the place takes no postposition.

items.pronunciation_notes: One short syllable with a clear e: der.

learn.title_en: देर is a noun, not an adjective
learn.explanation_en: English says I am late, with an adjective. Hindi says मुझे देर हो गई — lateness happened to me — with देर as a feminine noun. That difference produces three phrases worth learning whole: देर होना for being late, देर से for arriving late, and देर मत करो for do not delay. There is no adjective meaning late that describes a person, so the noun has to do all of it.

examples.note: गई is feminine, agreeing with देर.
The negative imperative with मत, from Module 7.
देर से is the standard way to say late as a manner.

common_error.why_en: That sentence says you are lateness itself. देर is a noun and it happens to you, so मुझे and होना.

practice.question: देर
practice.explanation_en: देर is lateness or delay, and it is a feminine noun rather than an adjective.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with देर when you are running late?
game.explanation_en: देर होना — lateness happens. देर करना means to delay something on purpose.

items.pronunciation_notes: Breathy ध in the middle, and both vowels are long: sii-dhaa.

learn.title_en: सीधा — the word directions are built on
learn.explanation_en: सीधा means straight, and it is a marked adjective, so it agrees: सीधा, सीधी, सीधे. As an instruction it is what you will be told when you ask the way — सीधे जाओ, go straight on, where the -े form is used adverbially. It also means straightforward or simple when describing a person or a problem, which is the same figurative jump English makes. This is the only marked adjective in the travel block, so it is the only one that requires a choice.

examples.note: The -े form works as an adverb here, describing how to go.
Agreeing with the masculine रास्ता.
Agreeing with the feminine सड़क — the same adjective, one letter different.

common_error.why_en: सड़क is feminine, so the marked adjective takes -ी. This is the payoff for flagging its gender two levels ago.

practice.question: सीधा
practice.explanation_en: सीधा is straight, and it also means straightforward when describing a person.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with सीधा in directions?
game.explanation_en: सीधे जाओ — go straight on. This is what you will be told when you ask the way.

summary.recap_en: The travel block is complete at fifteen words. Two things carry over: पहुँचना is intransitive so its whole tense grid is open to you, and देर is a noun rather than an adjective, so being late is something that happens to you rather than something you are.
summary.next_up_en: Next: health, and the vocabulary for saying what is wrong.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three syllables with the length on the middle one: ta-bii-yat.

learn.title_en: तबीयत — the word every health conversation starts with
learn.explanation_en: तबीयत is your physical condition, and तबीयत कैसी है is how Hindi asks whether someone is well. It is feminine and flagged, which shows up immediately in कैसी rather than कैसा. The standard way to say you are unwell is तबीयत ख़राब है — literally the condition is bad — where ख़राब is unmarked and never changes. There is no adjective meaning ill that describes the person directly, so this noun does the work.

examples.note: कैसी is feminine, agreeing with तबीयत.
मेरी is feminine too — the whole phrase agrees.
ठीक is unmarked and means all right or fine.

common_error.why_en: तबीयत is feminine, so the possessive is मेरी. The consonant ending predicts nothing.

practice.question: तबीयत
practice.explanation_en: तबीयत is your physical condition, and it is feminine.

game.question_en: Which adjective goes with तबीयत to say you are unwell?
game.explanation_en: तबीयत ख़राब है — the condition is bad. ख़राब is unmarked, so it never changes.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted ख़ is made far back in the throat, and the second syllable is long: bu-khaar.

learn.title_en: Fever happens to you, it is not something you have
learn.explanation_en: मुझे बुख़ार है means I have a fever, and it is built like every other body state in Hindi: the condition is the subject and the person takes को. So मुझे rather than मैं, and the verb agrees with बुख़ार. This is the same shape you learnt with ग़ुस्सा and ठंड, and once you have it, most of the health block builds itself. बुख़ार is masculine and flagged, and it is written with a dotted ख़.

examples.note: मुझे is मैं with को fused, from Module 6.
तेज़ means sharp or high, and था agrees with बुख़ार.
उतरना means to come down, and it is intransitive.

common_error.why_en: That sentence says you are a fever. The condition happens to you, so मुझे and a verb agreeing with बुख़ार.

practice.question: बुख़ार
practice.explanation_en: बुख़ार is fever, and it is masculine.

game.explanation_en: बुख़ार होना — fever happens to you, with the person marked by को.

items.pronunciation_notes: One syllable with the र rolled between the two d sounds: dard.

learn.title_en: Where it hurts goes in में
learn.explanation_en: दर्द is pain, masculine and flagged. To say where it hurts, the body part takes में: सिर में दर्द है, there is pain in the head, which is how Hindi says I have a headache. The person can be added with को if you need to be specific — मुझे सिर में दर्द है — but it is often left out because context makes it obvious. दर्द also carries the emotional sense of pain, exactly as in English.

examples.note: The basic shape, with the person marked by को.
The body part takes में, and सिर is oblique before it.

examples.hindi: पेट में दर्द हो रहा है
examples.read_as: peṭ meṁ dard ho rahaa hai
examples.note: The continuous, for pain happening right now.

common_error.why_en: The pain is located in the body part, so में is needed. The English possessive translates badly here.

practice.question: दर्द
practice.explanation_en: दर्द is pain, masculine, and it covers emotional pain too.

game.question_en: Which postposition marks where the दर्द is?
game.explanation_en: सिर में दर्द है — the body part takes में.

tts_strings: पेट में दर्द हो रहा है

summary.recap_en: Health in Hindi is built on one shape: the condition is the subject, the person takes को, and the body part takes में. तबीयत ख़राब है, मुझे बुख़ार है, सिर में दर्द है. No adjective describes the person directly, so these nouns do all the work.
summary.next_up_en: Next: medicine and the head, and a conversation about not feeling well.

items.pronunciation_notes: The first syllable is short and unstressed, the second long: da-vaa.

learn.title_en: The fourth feminine noun ending in -ा
learn.explanation_en: दवा is medicine, and it is feminine despite the -ा ending — joining चिंता, हवा and यात्रा. Four of them now, and they come from three different source languages, so the ending really is telling you nothing and the gender simply has to be memorised. The verb is लेना, to take, exactly as in English: दवा लो, take your medicine. लेना is transitive and its perfective लिया is still recognition only, so use the imperative or the future.

examples.note: The तुम imperative — लेना is transitive.
अच्छी is feminine, which proves दवा is.
The future, which is safe with any verb.

common_error.why_en: The -ा ending is misleading again. दवा is feminine, like चिंता, हवा and यात्रा.

practice.question: दवा
practice.explanation_en: दवा is medicine, and it is feminine despite ending in -ा.

game.explanation_en: दवा लेना — to take medicine, exactly as English says it.

items.pronunciation_notes: One short syllable, and the vowel is closer to the i in English 'sit' than to a long ee.

learn.title_en: सिर, and the body parts that go with it
learn.explanation_en: सिर is the head, masculine, flagged, and Class 2 so it never changes in the singular. It is the body part that turns up most in health complaints, and सिर में दर्द है is the everyday way to say I have a headache. There is a shorter form too — सिरदर्द, written as one word, meaning a headache as a thing. Both are common, and the longer version is the one that follows the general pattern from the last level.

examples.note: The body part takes में, as every complaint does.
दुखना is the verb to ache, and it is intransitive.
ठीक is unmarked and means all right.

common_error.why_en: सिर is masculine, so both the possessive and the verb are masculine. The short i makes it look like it might not be.

practice.question: सिर
practice.explanation_en: सिर is the head, and it is masculine.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with सिर when it aches?
game.explanation_en: सिर दुखना — the head aches. दुखना is intransitive, so the whole tense grid is available.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both words are stressed evenly, and ख़राब has the throaty ख़: kha-raab.

learn.title_en: Everything in this exchange agrees with तबीयत
learn.explanation_en: Four short lines, and the first two hang entirely on one fact: तबीयत is feminine. तुम्हारी, कैसी, मेरी — all three take -ी because of it, and a learner who guesses masculine gets three words wrong in a row rather than one. That is the practical reason gender is flagged and drilled. The second half of the exchange uses क्या हुआ from Module 7 and the को construction from the last level, so nothing here is new except the vocabulary.

common_error.why_en: तबीयत is feminine, so the possessive is मेरी. Getting the gender wrong here costs you three words in two lines.

practice.question: तबीयत ख़राब है
practice.explanation_en: Literally the condition is bad — the standard way to say you are unwell.

game.question_en: Listen to the second line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: तबीयत is feminine, so the possessive is मेरी.

summary.recap_en: दवा is the fourth feminine noun in this module ending in -ा, and the four come from three different source languages — so the ending genuinely predicts nothing and the gender has to be learnt. सिर में दर्द है is the pattern every health complaint follows.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the rest of the body-state words, including hunger and thirst, which behave the same way.
